---
title: "Software"
subtitle: "Interactive exercises for Quarto, running entirely in the browser"
---

The project's software turns ordinary [Quarto](https://quarto.org) course notes into
pages where students can practise. Python runs in the browser via
[Pyodide](https://pyodide.org) (WebAssembly): no server, no installation for students,
and no student data leaves the browser. AI feedback is optional.

All packages are open source (AGPL-3.0).

## For teachers: CTM Assessment

**[CTM Assessment](https://github.com/Erasmus-CTM/ctm-assessment)** is the package
you install. It brings writing, mathematics, Python and interactive diagrams together
on one page. Students try an idea, check their work and can ask for a hint.

[Try the examples](https://erasmus-ctm.github.io/ctm-assessment/example.html){.btn .btn-primary}
[Source and guide](https://github.com/Erasmus-CTM/ctm-assessment){.btn .btn-outline-secondary}

It contains these exercise types:

| Component | What students do | Try it |
|---|---|---|
| [math-exercise](https://github.com/Erasmus-CTM/math-exercise) | Enter a number, an expression, a vector or a matrix, or construct something on a diagram. Answers are checked symbolically (SymPy): equivalent, exact form, tolerance, sets. | [Examples](https://erasmus-ctm.github.io/math-exercise/) |
| [py-exercise](https://github.com/Erasmus-CTM/py-exercise) | Finish a small Python function and press *Check*. Hidden tests show what passes. | [Examples](https://erasmus-ctm.github.io/py-exercise/example.html) |
| [ctm-stack](https://github.com/Erasmus-CTM/ctm-stack) | Answer existing Moodle STACK questions on a Quarto page, graded in the browser. | [Examples](https://erasmus-ctm.github.io/ctm-stack/) |

: {.sm}

## Interactive Python cells: pyodide-interaktiv

**[pyodide-interaktiv](https://github.com/Erasmus-CTM/pyodide-interaktiv)** adds
editable Python cells to any Quarto page. Code runs in the background (Web Worker),
so the page stays responsive, and every cell can be stopped. Each cell can have an
AI feedback button. Without an API key it creates a ready-to-paste prompt instead.

```bash
quarto add Erasmus-CTM/pyodide-interaktiv
```

## Research prototypes

Work in progress that shows where the tools can go next.

| Repository | What it is |
|---|---|
| [stack-wasm-maxima](https://github.com/Erasmus-CTM/stack-wasm-maxima) | The computer algebra system Maxima compiled to WebAssembly, so STACK questions can be graded natively in the browser. [Comparison demo](https://erasmus-ctm.github.io/stack-wasm-maxima/) |
| [ctm_quiz_ltibff](https://github.com/Erasmus-CTM/ctm_quiz_ltibff) | Proof of concept: connecting a browser quiz to Canvas LMS via LTI. |
| [ctm_ai_eval](https://github.com/Erasmus-CTM/ctm_ai_eval) | Experiments on how to evaluate course chatbots (retrieval and answer quality). |

: {.sm}

## Building blocks

Shared libraries used by the packages above. Course authors do not install them
separately: [ctm-libs](https://github.com/Erasmus-CTM/ctm-libs) (settings, languages,
Python runtime, AI feedback) and
[ctm-checkers](https://github.com/Erasmus-CTM/ctm-checkers) (the Python grading code).
